title: Meta must pay and change its apps

paragraphs: Meta has agreed to pay an 18 billion-dollar (16.5 billion euros) settlement to resolve claims from 48 US states, Washington, D.C., and three territories.
The legal actions accused Facebook and Instagram of harming children’s mental health through addictive features.

Although Meta denied any wrongdoing, the company agreed to pay the sum in annual instalments over a 10-year period to avoid potentially higher fines. Beyond the financial settlement, Meta will introduce significant online safety features for teenage users. These include a default two-hour daily time limit, automatic night-time blocks between midnight and 6:00 AM, and restrictions during school hours. Additionally, Meta plans to hide like counts and photo filters that simulate cosmetic surgery.
However, Meta insists that 30% of the funds will only be released if competitors like TikTok and YouTube adopt similar safety restrictions, which started a debate about industry-wide accountability.

paragraphs: The company Meta agreed to pay a big settlement of 18 billion dollars (16.5 billion euros) to 48 American states. US officials accused Facebook and Instagram of harming the health of children.

Meta said it didn’t do anything wrong, but the company agreed to pay the money over ten years. Meta will also add new safety rules for teenagers on Facebook and Instagram. Teenagers will have a two-hour daily time limit, and the apps will be blocked at night and during school hours. Meta will also hide the number of likes on posts to help young people feel better.
Meta wants other big companies, like TikTok and YouTube, to follow these new safety rules as well to make the internet safer for all children.
